# MenuBar

Header: `winui/ui/menus/MenuBar.hpp`. Spec: `winui/ui/menus/MenuBar.hpp`.

A horizontal menu bar: a row of headers, each dropping down a cascading MenuFlyout-style menu that floats in the overlay layer under the header's left edge.

The bar is one tab stop. Left/Right move between headers and wrap around. Down, Enter and Space open the focused header's menu with its first item focused. While a menu is open the bar keeps focus and passes the keys on to the menu. Every item's shortcut fires app-wide, whether its menu is open or not. The declarative form is [ui::MenuBar](#uimenubar).

Example: 
```cpp
bool show_status_bar = true;
auto menu = std::make_unique<ui::MenuBarControl>();
menu->set_items({
    ui::MenuBarItem{.text = "File", .items = {
        {.text = "Open", .shortcut = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::O, .on_click = [&] { open_file(); }},
        ui::MenuItem::separator(),
        {.text = "Exit", .on_click = [&] { quit(); }},
    }},
    ui::MenuBarItem{.text = "View", .items = {
        ui::MenuItem::toggle("Status bar", /*checked=*/true,
                                      [&](bool on) { show_status_bar = on; }),
    }},
});

auto stack = std::make_unique<ui::StackControl>(ui::Orientation::Vertical);
ui::MenuBarControl* bar = stack->add(std::move(menu)); // observer; the stack owns it
window.set_content(std::move(stack));

// Or declaratively:
window.set_content(ui::MenuBar{ .items = {
    { .text = "File", .items = { { .text = "Open", .on_click = [&] { open_file(); } },
                                 ui::MenuItem::separator(),
                                 { .text = "Exit", .on_click = [&] { quit(); } } } },
}});
```

## `ui::MenuBar`

A menu bar. Builds a [ui::MenuBarControl](#uimenubarcontrol). Each menu is a list of [ui::MenuItem](menu-flyout.md#struct-menuitem), so its items may be toggles, radio items, separators or submenus with icons and shortcuts. Every item's shortcut fires app-wide, whether its menu is open or not.

Menu items live in a std::vector built from a brace list, which only copies, so [ui::MenuItem::on_click](menu-flyout.md#on_click) is a copyable std::function. A handler must not capture a move-only value.

Example: 
```cpp
ui::Property<bool> status_bar{true};
window.set_content(ui::VerticalStack{ .content = {
    ui::MenuBar{ .items = {
        { .text  = "File",
          .items = { { .text = "Open", .shortcut = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::O,
                       .on_click = [&] { open_file(); } },
                     ui::MenuItem::separator(),
                     { .text = "Exit", .on_click = [&] { quit(); } } } },
        { .text  = "View",
          .items = { ui::MenuItem::toggle("Status bar", ui::bind(status_bar)) } },
    }},
    ui::Text{ .text = "Document" },
}});
```

Every field, in the order a designated initializer names them:

```cpp
ui::MenuBar{
    .items, .style, .margin, .width, .height, .min_width, .min_height, .max_width, .max_height,
    .horizontal_alignment, .vertical_alignment, .visible, .tool_tip, .enabled, .accessibility,
    .on_pointer_entered, .on_pointer_exited, .on_got_focus, .on_lost_focus, .on_key_down,
    .on_wheel, .control
}
```

Fields, in declaration order (designators must follow it):

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| <span id="uimenubar-items"></span>`items` | `ui::Binding<std::vector<ui::MenuBarItem>>` |  | The bar's headers, left to right, each with the menu it drops down. |
| <span id="uimenubar-on_pointer_entered"></span>`on_pointer_entered` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer moved onto the control. |
| <span id="uimenubar-on_pointer_exited"></span>`on_pointer_exited` | `ui::Action` |  | The pointer left the control. |
| <span id="uimenubar-on_got_focus"></span>`on_got_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus arrived on the control, or on anything inside it, from outside it. A control with nothing focusable in it never gets focus, and never raises this. |
| <span id="uimenubar-on_lost_focus"></span>`on_lost_focus` | `ui::Action` |  | Keyboard focus left the control and everything inside it. |
| <span id="uimenubar-on_key_down"></span>`on_key_down` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::KeyEvent&)>` |  | A key pressed while focus is on the control or inside it, before the control's own handling; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_key_down()](../tree/element.md#on_key_down)). |
| <span id="uimenubar-on_wheel"></span>`on_wheel` | `ui::Callback<ui::Handling(const ui::PointerEvent&)>` |  | A wheel turn over the control, before the control scrolls; [ui::Handled](../core/namespace-ui.md#handled) stops it there ([Element::on_wheel()](../tree/element.md#on_wheel)). |
| <span id="uimenubar-control"></span>`control` | `ui::ControlOut<ui::MenuBar>` |  | Out: the handle that receives the built control. |

Plus the common fields `style`, `margin`, `width`, `height`, `min_width`, `min_height`, `max_width`, `max_height`, `horizontal_alignment`, `vertical_alignment`, `visible`, `tool_tip`, `enabled`, `accessibility` every spec carries ([conventions](../conventions.md#common-fields-on-every-spec)).

### items

```cpp
const std::vector<MenuBarItem>& items() const
```

The menus, in header order. Toggle and radio items' is_checked() reflect clicks made in the open menu and the properties their `checked` is bound to, so read them back from here.

### set_items

```cpp
void set_items(std::vector<MenuBarItem> items)
```

Replaces the menus, closes any that is open and lays out the header row again.

### open_index

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> open_index() const
```

Which header's menu is open; unset when none is.

### active_command

```cpp
std::optional<std::size_t> active_command() const
```

The item holding focus in the open menu (an index into its top level); unset when there is none.

### focused_header

```cpp
std::size_t focused_header() const
```

The header the keyboard is on (Left/Right move it); 0 for a fresh bar.

### open

```cpp
void open(std::size_t index, bool from_keyboard = false)
```

Opens header `index`'s menu, as a click on it would, closing any other. With `from_keyboard` the menu's first focusable item is focused, as Down/Enter/Space do. Does nothing for an out-of-range index or a disabled bar; a header with an empty menu only takes the keyboard focus.

### close

```cpp
void close()
```

Closes the open menu and its submenus. The menu fades out over the theme's close duration.

### focused

```cpp
bool focused() const
```

Whether the bar holds keyboard focus; the focus ring is then drawn around [focused_header()](#focused_header).

### focusable

```cpp
bool focusable() const override
```

One tab stop for the whole bar, while it is enabled and has at least one header.

### handle_global_shortcut

```cpp
bool handle_global_shortcut(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Every menu's shortcuts, open or not.

### take_menu_access

```cpp
bool take_menu_access(char32_t letter) override
```

Alt or F10 alone moves keyboard focus to the first header. Alt with a letter opens the menu whose header starts with that letter, ignoring case, with its first item focused. Escape and running an item give focus back ([Window::end_menu_access()](../tree/window.md#end_menu_access)).

### transition_opacity

```cpp
float transition_opacity() const override
```

The menu's opacity: fully opaque while it slides in, then fading out as it closes.

### measure_override

```cpp
Size measure_override(Size available, const MeasureContext& context) const override
```

The header row. Each header is its title plus padding and margin, and the bar is at least 40 DIPs tall. An open menu floats and never changes this size.

### arrange_override

```cpp
void arrange_override(const Rect& final_rect, const ArrangeContext& context) override
```

Keeps an open menu hanging from its header.

### pointer_override

```cpp
bool pointer_override(const PointerEvent& e) override
```

Hover highlights a header; a click opens its menu, and a second click on the same header closes it. While a menu is open, moving onto another header opens that one instead.

### render_override

```cpp
void render_override(Renderer& renderer, const RenderContext& context) const override
```

Draws the header row: subtle header backgrounds, the open menu's header pressed-in, and the focus ring around the focused header. The menu itself is a popup the window draws.

### tick_override

```cpp
void tick_override(Duration delta) override
```

Advances the menu's open slide, submenu hover delays and the close fade.

### clear_dirty_override

```cpp
void clear_dirty_override(DirtyFlags flags) override
```

Clears the bar's dirty flags and those of the floating menu with it.

### enabled_changed

```cpp
void enabled_changed() override
```

[is_enabled()](../tree/element.md#is_enabled) flipped, through [set_enabled()](../tree/element.md#set_enabled) here or on an ancestor, or a move to another parent. Drop any press or hover state. The element is redrawn either way. No-op by default.

### focus_changed

```cpp
void focus_changed(bool focused) override
```

Called by the [Window](../tree/window.md) as focus arrives or leaves; losing focus closes the open menu.

### key_override

```cpp
bool key_override(const KeyEvent& e) override
```

Left/Right move between headers. With a menu open, they move into the neighboring menu when the open menu has no use for the key. Down, Enter and Space open the focused header's menu, and while a menu is open its keys go to it.

### focus_ring_rect

```cpp
Rect focus_ring_rect(const Theme&) const override
```

Around the focused header.

## struct MenuBarItem

One top-level entry of a Menu bar: the header title and the items of the menu that drops down from it.

Example: 
```cpp
auto menu = std::make_unique<ui::MenuBarControl>();
ui::MenuBarItem file{.text = "File", .items = {
    {.text = "Open", .shortcut = ui::Ctrl + ui::Key::O, .on_click = [&] { open_file(); }},
    ui::MenuItem::separator(),
    {.text = "Exit", .on_click = [&] { quit(); }},
}};
menu->set_items({std::move(file)});
```

| Field | Type | Default | |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `text` | `std::string` |  | The header title shown in the bar. |
| `items` | `std::vector<MenuItem>` |  | The menu's entries; they may be toggles, radio items, separators and submenus. |
